photos.groupLabel: Easy: portraits
photos.title: [Portrait of Harriet Tubman]
photos.description: Harriet Tubman stands facing the camera in a black-and-white full-length studio portrait. She wears a dark, long-sleeved dress with a row of buttons down the bodice and a white ruffled collar. Her hands are clasped on the back of an upholstered chair with fringe and a hanging tassel, and a dark garment is draped over the chair. A small table with a cloth stands at the left, with a plain studio wall and vertical trim behind her.

Remains of War of 1812 fort which later became the famous Castle Garden, theatre and emigrant landing depot, and finally, the New York City Aquarium. Restoration of fort ruins began in October 1950. Work will continue as funds are available. - National Park Service United States Dept. of Interior".

photos.title: Bird's-eye view of Philadelphia / drawn and engraved expressly for Harper's Weekly from sketches by Theodore R. Davis.
photos.description: A panoramic bird's-eye engraving titled 'BIRD'S-EYE VIEW OF PHILADELPHIA,' with a top banner reading 'SUPPLEMENT TO HARPER'S WEEKLY, JUNE 15, 1872' and side notes 'Drawn and Engraved Expressly for Harper's Weekly' and 'From Sketches by Theodore R. Davis.' The city fills most of the image as a vast grid of streets and blocks, with a wide river and wharves in the foreground, boats on the water, and small islands or landforms near the bottom. Rows of buildings, open squares, and a few larger structures are visible across the dense grid, while the far edge fades into open land and low hills under a plain sky. Individual people are not distinguishable.

photos.title: View of the ruins of the city of Pittsburgh from Boyd's Hill / painted by W.C. Wall ; on stone by James Queen ; lith. of Wagner & McGuigan, No. 100, Chesnut Street, Philada.
photos.description: A lithograph titled 'VIEW OF THE RUINS of the CITY of PITTSBURGH from BOYD'S HILL,' with credits reading 'Painted by W.C. Wall,' 'Lith. of Wagner & McGuigan, No. 100, Chesnut Street, Philada.,' and 'On Stone by James Queen.' It looks down from a hill over a city of ruined buildings: many walls stand roofless, with empty window openings and tall chimneys rising above the rubble. A broad street runs into the distance, with small figures walking on and near it, and a river and wooded hills lie beyond the ruined blocks. In the foreground, a curved path or road leads down from the hill, with a few people.
